senses.gloss: , Hif. הִתְרָה (sec. r. of ראה, cmp. זָהַר Hif.) to forewarn, esp. to inform a person about to commit a criminal act of the penalty which he will incur.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 5:1">Snh. V, 1</cite> (to witnesses) <he>הִתְרֵיתֶם בו</he> have you warned him? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 40b:19">Ib. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>התריתם בו קיבל עליו וכ׳</he> did you warn him? did he accept the warning? did he surrender &c.?, v. <cite ref="N01392"><he>נָתַר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Sanhedrin 11:1">Tosef. ib. XI, 1</cite> <he>בין שהִיתְרוּ בו כל וכ׳</he> whether all the witnesses against him or a part of them had warned him; <he>עד שיַתְרוּ בו כל עדיו</he> (he cannot be punished,) unless all his witnesses had warned him. Ib. 2 <he>מַתְרִין בו ושותק וכ׳</he> if they warn him, and he keeps silence &c.

<cite ref="Numbers 15:33">Num. XV, 33</cite>) <he>מגיד שהתרו בו מעין מלאכתו</he> this intimates that they warned him, mentioning the nature of his labor (the category under which it comes), <he>מכאן … שמַתְרִים בהם וכ׳</he> from this we learn that in all cases of principal labors intimated in the Torah warning must be given and the category must be defined.
<cite ref="Numbers 15:33">Ib.</cite> <he>מלמד שהתרו בו וכ׳</he> this shows that they warned him (to stop), and then (when he persisted) they brought him before Moses.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 9b:2">Snh. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>שהיתרו בה אחרים ולא היתרו וכ׳</he> when others had warned her, but the witnesses had not; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מוּתְרֶה</he>, pl. <he>מוּתְרִים</he>, <he>מוּתְרִין</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 109b">B. Mets. 109ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 21b">B. Bath. 21ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U02122"><he>שַׁתָּלָא</he></cite>.
